title: Orchard and Uniform
premise: Juniper Ashgrove, a widowed lighthouse keeper on the storm-battered island of Merrow's Reach, has spent his life measuring what can be carried — grief, oil, duty. When the great storms of 1893 close the tidal bridge for an entire season, he becomes the only witness to a smuggling ring run by the garrison commander, whose stolen grain is being sold while the island starves. Juniper must smuggle the truth itself off the island in his logbooks before the victors' historians arrive to write the official record, choosing between loyalty to the found family of islanders who sheltered him and obedience to the uniformed men he once trusted. He ends the season by testifying at the inquiry, keeping the lighthouse lit through the worst storm in living memory, and inheriting not land but the community that finally claims him as its own.
about_author: Noor Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logbooks along the northern coast. Orchard and Uniform is their second novel, following the acclaimed The Salt Inheritance.

chapters.title: The Weight of Oil
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Opening in autumn 1893, Juniper trims the lamp, rations his stores, and measures his late wife's belongings for what can be carried. Establishes his grief and precision. Emotional beat: quiet endurance masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: A naval cutter delivers sealed orders: the bridge will close for the season due to storm damage, and garrison commander Captain Ellery Voss assumes authority over the island. Juniper's POV; first unease as Voss requisitions the harvest stores. Beat: dread beneath formality.

chapters.title: The Orchard Keepers
chapters.summary: Juniper descends to the village and meets the Hallow family — orchard farmers Maren and her son Tam — who feed him and fold him into supper without ceremony. His POV. Found-family thread begins. Beat: warmth he resists and craves.

chapters.title: Grain That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The ration ledger shows grain issued that never reached the village tables. Maren suspects Voss but says nothing aloud. Beat: suspicion sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: A Light on the Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. From the gallery he spots an unlit supply sloop landing at the cove at night — off the official schedule. He logs it honestly, then hesitates over whether to report it. Beat: the first crack between duty and truth.

chapters.title: Tam's Errand
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Sent to the garrison with a petition, fourteen-year-old Tam witnesses crates of grain being loaded onto a private boat and is threatened by a sergeant. Beat: innocence colliding with menace.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He copies his logbook pages into a hidden second ledger, echoing his habit of measuring what can be carried — now carrying evidence instead of possessions. Beat: resolve forming.

chapters.title: Voss Comes to Dinner
chapters.summary: Alternating Juniper/Maren. Voss dines at the Hallows', charming and menacing, probing who has been asking questions about the cove. Beat: civility as a weapon; loyalty tested in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Sergeant's Confession
chapters.summary: Sergeant Brandt, drunk and ashamed, finds Juniper at the lighthouse and half-confesses the scheme — grain sold to mainland brokers while the island starves. Juniper's POV. Beat: pity for a man complicit in hunger.

chapters.title: First Storm
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Juniper's POV. The season's first great storm hits; the light must be kept burning through the night while the village floods below. Beat: the keeper's duty as metaphor — holding steady when everything shakes.

chapters.title: Hunger in the Rows
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Winter deepens; children go hungry while garrison tables stay full. The village council debates confronting Voss; Maren argues for patience and proof. Beat: moral tension between action and evidence.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Official word arrives: no boats, no post, no escape until spring. The island is sealed with its secret. Juniper realizes his hidden ledger may be the only record that survives. Beat: claustrophobia and stakes crystallizing.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Cove
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam tries to mark the smugglers' boat and is caught; Voss uses him as leverage, warning the village that troublemakers' families will lose rations entirely. Beat: guilt and fury; loyalty strained to breaking.

chapters.title: The Historian's Shadow
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A letter reveals a mainland historian will arrive in spring to compile the official account of the season — written from Voss's reports alone. Time pressure made explicit. Beat: urgency; truth racing against ink.

chapters.title: Brandt's Choice
chapters.summary: Sergeant Brandt's POV. Torn between oath and conscience, Brandt brings Juniper the shipping manifests — then disappears, arrested by his own men. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What Maren Knew
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She reveals she has known since autumn and stayed silent to protect Tam; her confession shames and steadies Juniper. They merge her testimony with his ledger. Beat: forgiveness and partnership.

chapters.title: The Raid on the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Voss's soldiers search the lighthouse for the ledger. Juniper hides it inside the lens housing, among the very machinery of the light. Beat: terror and ingenuity; the light literally guarding the truth.

chapters.title: The Great Storm
chapters.summary: Climax part one, ensemble. The worst storm in living memory strikes; a garrison supply ship founders on the rocks. Juniper keeps the light burning through the night, saving the same sailors sent to silence him. Beat: heroism without hatred.

chapters.title: Testimony by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Juniper's POV. Shipwrecked sailors, led by Brandt (escaped during the chaos), corroborate the ledger before the surviving officers. Voss's authority collapses in the flooded garrison hall. Beat: truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The bridge reopens; the inquiry historian arrives and takes Juniper's sworn statement alongside the villagers'. Voss is taken to the mainland for trial. Beat: vindication, quiet rather than triumphant.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The Hallows formally offer Juniper a share of the orchard and a room in their house — an inheritance chosen, not inherited. He buries his wife's packed trunk unopened, finally home. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: The Record Stands
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue. A year later, the published history carries the true account; Juniper reads it aloud to Tam in the lantern room and enters one last line in his logbook: all accounted for. Beat: peace; the light still burning.
